title: Benchmark contamination
bottleneck: Benchmark questions leak into training corpora at web scale, so high scores may reflect memorization rather than capability — and nobody can reliably detect the leakage. Models train on data that includes test sets, posted solutions, and near-duplicates; decontamination via n-gram filtering misses paraphrases. The result is an evaluation ecosystem where measured progress may be partly illusory. Once test items leak into training data, scores measure memorization - and contamination is effectively undetectable at web scale.
why_it_blocks: If benchmarks measure recall of leaked answers, then the entire narrative of AI progress — and the deployment decisions based on it — rests on inflated numbers.
current_state: LiveCodeBench and similar post-cutoff benchmarks fight contamination with fresh problems, but the arms race favors the leakers; most legacy benchmarks are likely contaminated.
